notes.summary: The opening asks when a family of component figures F_i arises from one global figure. C4 asserts compatibility for elements in disjoint connected components of M. The inserted note calls this necessary and sufficient for the following corollaries. Corollary 1 concerns the image of the component map and contains a revised, still awkward support condition. Corollary 2 is revised to the finite-index case. Corollary 3 states a finite-type (respectively finite) inheritance assertion and describes the image by an eventual-empty condition.
math_reading_decisions: The component question might suggest a plain terminal F, but a low loop remains visible; the F_0/F uncertainty is retained.
The two bars after en est de are literally transcribed as =; their likely verbal function is recorded only in the abbreviation table.
The third component-map connector lacks a complete head. Expected map notation does not justify converting it to a definite arrow.
The cancelled pres in Corollary 1 creates an awkward live ending. H’s replacement un nb fini d’i was rejected because those letters are absent; no mathematical repair was made.
The page does not supply the preceding definitions or proof details needed to validate the corollaries. No independent proof or computation was performed.
author_checks: The explicit question is: « quand peut-on dire qu'il existe F … ? » (the complete wording is retained in the transcription).
The interlinear phrase reads « C'est néc et suffisant pour la [validité, state uncertain] des »; this is an author assertion, not a verified implication in this run.
Two draft cases are struck: « a) I est fini » and « b) Toute figure est de t.f. -- alors ». The replacement Cor. 2 keeps the finite-index case.
